agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

{

        index=$((index+1))
    done
    index=-1
}

}

// setNoOpt makes a boolean flag accept an optional value (--flag[=true|false]).

	}
	fl.NoOptDefVal = "true"
}

func NewTerminfoScreenFromTtyTerminfo(tty Tty, ti *terminfo.Terminfo) (s Screen, e error) {
	term := defaultTerm
	if term == "" {
		term = os.Getenv("TERM")
	}
	if ti == nil {
		ti, e = LookupTerminfo(term)
		if e != nil {

		}

	t := &tScreen{ti: ti, tty: tty}

	if len(ti.Mouse) > 0 {

	}
	t.prepareKeys()
	t.buildAcsMap()
	t.resizeQ = make(chan bool, 1)
	t.fallback = make(map[rune]string)
	maps.Copy(t.fallback, RuneFallbacks)

	return &baseScreen{screenImpl: t}, nil
}

// NewKeyBind merges the configured key bindings with the defaults.
func NewKeyBind(cfg map[string][]string) KeyBind {
	return newKeyBind(cfg, false)
}

// NewKeyBindWithDefault builds the key bindings; when disableDefault is
// true only the configured key bindings are used.
func NewKeyBindWithDefault(cfg map[string][]string, disableDefault bool) KeyBind {
	return newKeyBind(cfg, disableDefault)
}

func newKeyBind(cfg map[string][]string, disableDefault bool) KeyBind {
	kb := KeyBind{}
	if !disableDefault {
		kb = defaultKeyBinds()
	} else {
		for k := range defaultKeyBinds() {
			kb[k] = nil
		}
	}
	for k, v := range cfg {
		kb[k] = v
	}
	return kb
}

// KeyBindHelp returns the key binding help text.
func KeyBindHelp(kb KeyBind) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("ov is a feature rich pager\n")
	b.WriteString(" Key                            Action\n")
	for _, g := range keyHelpGroups {
		b.WriteString("\n\t" + g.title + "\n")
		for _, e := range g.entries {
			b.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf(" %-30s * %s\n", keyList(kb[e.action]), e.desc))
		}
	}
	return b.String()
}

func keyList(keys []string) string {
	if len(keys) == 0 {
		return "[]"
	}
	parts := make([]string, len(keys))
	for i, k := range keys {
		parts[i] = "[" + k + "]"
	}
	return strings.Join(parts, ", ")
}

// keyEvent is a normalized representation of a key press.
type keyEvent struct {
	key tcell.Key
	ch  rune
	mod tcell.ModMask
}

// keyMap maps normalized key events to action names.
type keyMap map[keyEvent]string

// errInvalidKey is returned when a key name can not be parsed.
var errInvalidKey = fmt.Errorf("invalid key event")

var specialKeys = map[string]tcell.Key{
	"enter":     tcell.KeyEnter,
	"backspace": tcell.KeyBackspace2,
	"tab":       tcell.KeyTab,
	"backtab":   tcell.KeyBacktab,
	"esc":       tcell.KeyEscape,
	"escape":    tcell.KeyEscape,
	"delete":    tcell.KeyDelete,
	"insert":    tcell.KeyInsert,
	"up":        tcell.KeyUp,
	"down":      tcell.KeyDown,
	"left":      tcell.KeyLeft,
	"right":     tcell.KeyRight,
	"home":      tcell.KeyHome,
	"end":       tcell.KeyEnd,
	"pageup":    tcell.KeyPgUp,
	"pgup":      tcell.KeyPgUp,
	"pagedown":  tcell.KeyPgDn,
	"pgdn":      tcell.KeyPgDn,
	"space":     ' ',
	"clear":     tcell.KeyClear,
	"exit":      tcell.KeyExit,
	"cancel":    tcell.KeyCancel,
	"print":     tcell.KeyPrint,
	"pause":     tcell.KeyPause,
	"help":      tcell.KeyHelp,
	"center":    tcell.KeyCenter,
}

// parseKeyName converts a key name such as "ctrl+alt+c" into a keyEvent.
func parseKeyName(name string) (keyEvent, error) {
	var mod tcell.ModMask
	ev := keyEvent{}
	parts := strings.Split(name, "+")
	// A trailing "+" means the key is '+' itself.
	if strings.HasSuffix(name, "+") {
		parts = parts[:len(parts)-1]
		parts = append(parts, "+")
	}
	keyName := parts[len(parts)-1]
	for _, m := range parts[:len(parts)-1] {
		switch strings.ToLower(m) {
		case "ctrl", "control":
			mod |= tcell.ModCtrl
		case "alt":
			mod |= tcell.ModAlt
		case "meta":
			mod |= tcell.ModMeta
		case "shift":
			mod |= tcell.ModShift
		default:
			return ev, errInvalidKey
		}
	}
	lower := strings.ToLower(keyName)
	if k, ok := specialKeys[lower]; ok {
		if lower == "space" {
			ev.key = tcell.KeyRune
			ev.ch = ' '
		} else {
			ev.key = k
		}
		ev.mod = mod
		return normalizeKey(ev), nil
	}
	if len(lower) >= 2 && lower[0] == 'f' {
		if n, err := strconv.Atoi(lower[1:]); err == nil && n >= 1 && n <= 64 {
			ev.key = tcell.Key(int(tcell.KeyF1) + n - 1)
			ev.mod = mod
			return normalizeKey(ev), nil
		}
	}
	r := []rune(keyName)
	if len(r) != 1 {
		return ev, errInvalidKey
	}
	ev.key = tcell.KeyRune
	ev.ch = r[0]
	ev.mod = mod
	return normalizeKey(ev), nil
}

// normalizeKey canonicalizes ctrl+letter combinations to tcell control keys,
// mirroring how tcell reports them.
func normalizeKey(ev keyEvent) keyEvent {
	if ev.key == tcell.KeyRune && ev.mod&tcell.ModCtrl != 0 {
		c := ev.ch
		if c >= 'a' && c <= 'z' {
			c = c - 'a' + 'A'
		}
		if c >= '@' && c <= '_' {
			ev.key = tcell.Key(c - '@')
			ev.ch = 0
			ev.mod &^= tcell.ModCtrl
		}
	}
	if ev.key == tcell.KeyRune && ev.mod&tcell.ModShift != 0 {
		// shift is implied by the rune itself.
		ev.mod &^= tcell.ModShift
	}
	return ev
}

// keyEventFromTcell converts a tcell event into the normalized form.
func keyEventFromTcell(ev *tcell.EventKey) keyEvent {
	ke := keyEvent{key: ev.Key(), ch: ev.Rune(), mod: ev.Modifiers()}
	if ke.key == tcell.KeyRune {
		ke.mod &^= tcell.ModShift
	} else {
		ke.ch = 0
	}
	// tcell reports ctrl+letter as a control key with ModCtrl set.
	if ke.key >= tcell.KeyCtrlA && ke.key <= tcell.KeyCtrlUnderscore {
		ke.mod &^= tcell.ModCtrl
	}
	if ke.key == tcell.KeyBackspace {
		ke.key = tcell.KeyBackspace2
	}
	return ke
}

// buildKeyMap compiles the key bindings into a lookup map.
// Only the actions listed in filter (if non-nil) are included.
func buildKeyMap(kb KeyBind, include func(action string) bool) (keyMap, error) {
	km := keyMap{}
	for _, g := range keyHelpGroups {
		for _, e := range g.entries {
			if include != nil && !include(e.action) {
				continue
			}
			for _, name := range kb[e.action] {
				ke, err := parseKeyName(name)
				if err != nil {
					return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to set key bindings [%s] for %s: %w", name, e.action, err)
				}
				km[ke] = e.action
			}
		}
	}
	return km, nil
}

func isInputAction(action string) bool {
	return strings.HasPrefix(action, "input_")
}
EOF
echo ok"}

// NewKeyBind merges the configured key bindings with the defaults.
func NewKeyBind(cfg map[string][]string) KeyBind {
	return newKeyBind(cfg, false)
}

// NewKeyBindWithDefault builds the key bindings; when disableDefault is
// true only the configured key bindings are used.
func NewKeyBindWithDefault(cfg map[string][]string, disableDefault bool) KeyBind {
	return newKeyBind(cfg, disableDefault)
}

func newKeyBind(cfg map[string][]string, disableDefault bool) KeyBind {
	kb := KeyBind{}
	if !disableDefault {
		kb = defaultKeyBinds()
	} else {
		for k := range defaultKeyBinds() {
			kb[k] = nil
		}
	}
	for k, v := range cfg {
		kb[k] = v
	}
	return kb
}

// KeyBindHelp returns the key binding help text.
func KeyBindHelp(kb KeyBind) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("ov is a feature rich pager\n")
	b.WriteString(" Key                            Action\n")
	for _, g := range keyHelpGroups {
		b.WriteString("\n\t" + g.title + "\n")
		for _, e := range g.entries {
			b.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf(" %-30s * %s\n", keyList(kb[e.action]), e.desc))
		}
	}
	return b.String()
}

func keyList(keys []string) string {
	if len(keys) == 0 {
		return "[]"
	}
	parts := make([]string, len(keys))
	for i, k := range keys {
		parts[i] = "[" + k + "]"
	}
	return strings.Join(parts, ", ")
}

// parseKeyName converts a key name such as "ctrl+alt+c" into a keyEvent.
func parseKeyName(name string) (keyEvent, error) {
	var mod tcell.ModMask
	ev := keyEvent{}
	parts := strings.Split(name, "+")
	// A trailing "+" means the key is '+' itself.
	if strings.HasSuffix(name, "+") {
		parts = parts[:len(parts)-1]
		parts = append(parts, "+")
	}
	keyName := parts[len(parts)-1]
	for _, m := range parts[:len(parts)-1] {
		switch strings.ToLower(m) {
		case "ctrl", "control":
			mod |= tcell.ModCtrl
		case "alt":
			mod |= tcell.ModAlt
		case "meta":
			mod |= tcell.ModMeta
		case "shift":
			mod |= tcell.ModShift
		default:
			return ev, errInvalidKey
		}
	}
	lower := strings.ToLower(keyName)
	if k, ok := specialKeys[lower]; ok {
		if lower == "space" {
			ev.key = tcell.KeyRune
			ev.ch = ' '
		} else {
			ev.key = k
		}
		ev.mod = mod
		return normalizeKey(ev), nil
	}
	if len(lower) >= 2 && lower[0] == 'f' {
		if n, err := strconv.Atoi(lower[1:]); err == nil && n >= 1 && n <= 64 {
			ev.key = tcell.Key(int(tcell.KeyF1) + n - 1)
			ev.mod = mod
			return normalizeKey(ev), nil
		}
	}
	r := []rune(keyName)
	if len(r) != 1 {
		return ev, errInvalidKey
	}
	ev.key = tcell.KeyRune
	ev.ch = r[0]
	ev.mod = mod
	return normalizeKey(ev), nil
}

// normalizeKey canonicalizes ctrl+letter combinations to tcell control keys,
// mirroring how tcell reports them.
func normalizeKey(ev keyEvent) keyEvent {
	if ev.key == tcell.KeyRune && ev.mod&tcell.ModCtrl != 0 {
		c := ev.ch
		if c >= 'a' && c <= 'z' {
			c = c - 'a' + 'A'
		}
		if c >= '@' && c <= '_' {
			ev.key = tcell.Key(c - '@')
			ev.ch = 0
			ev.mod &^= tcell.ModCtrl
		}
	}
	if ev.key == tcell.KeyRune && ev.mod&tcell.ModShift != 0 {
		// shift is implied by the rune itself.
		ev.mod &^= tcell.ModShift
	}
	return ev
}

// keyEventFromTcell converts a tcell event into the normalized form.
func keyEventFromTcell(ev *tcell.EventKey) keyEvent {
	ke := keyEvent{key: ev.Key(), ch: ev.Rune(), mod: ev.Modifiers()}
	if ke.key == tcell.KeyRune {
		ke.mod &^= tcell.ModShift
	} else {
		ke.ch = 0
	}
	// tcell reports ctrl+letter as a control key with ModCtrl set.
	if ke.key >= tcell.KeyCtrlA && ke.key <= tcell.KeyCtrlUnderscore {
		ke.mod &^= tcell.ModCtrl
	}
	if ke.key == tcell.KeyBackspace {
		ke.key = tcell.KeyBackspace2
	}
	return ke
}

// buildKeyMap compiles the key bindings into a lookup map.
// Only the actions listed in filter (if non-nil) are included.
func buildKeyMap(kb KeyBind, include func(action string) bool) (keyMap, error) {
	km := keyMap{}
	for _, g := range keyHelpGroups {
		for _, e := range g.entries {
			if include != nil && !include(e.action) {
				continue
			}
			for _, name := range kb[e.action] {
				ke, err := parseKeyName(name)
				if err != nil {
					return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to set key bindings [%s] for %s: %w", name, e.action, err)
				}
				km[ke] = e.action
			}
		}
	}
	return km, nil
}

func isInputAction(action string) bool {
	return strings.HasPrefix(action, "input_")
}
